recipes.name: Kichaloo Banjan - Afghan Potato Eggplant Dish
instructions: Trim the tops off the eggplants. Optionally, use a potato peeler to create a decorative striped pattern by peeling alternating lengthwise strips of the skin.
Slice the eggplant into ½-inch (1½ cm) rounds and place them in a large bowl. Sprinkle with salt and massage it onto both sides of each slice.

Let the eggplant sit for 2 to 4 hours to draw out excess moisture. By the end, it should be "sweating" with a pool of dark liquid collected at the bottom of the bowl. This helps reduce oil absorption later.
Use a clean kitchen towel to squeeze out as much moisture as possible from each eggplant slice.

Heat half the oil in a sauté pan over high heat. Once hot, reduce to medium and add half the eggplant in a single layer. Fry until golden on both sides, then transfer to a plate. Repeat with the remaining oil and eggplant.
Once the last batch of eggplant is golden on both sides, reduce the heat to low and layer the sliced potatoes, tomatoes, and cooked eggplant in the pan.
Meanwhile, heat the oil and garlic in a small pan over medium-high heat. Cook for about 3 minutes, or until the garlic turns golden.
Then add the turmeric and salt, stirring for 20 seconds.
Add the boiling water and stir to dissolve the turmeric. Then pour the mixture over the vegetables in the sauté pan.

Cover and cook over medium-low heat for 35 to 40 minutes without stirring, as this will keep the vegetables from turning to mush. Serve with a drizzle of garlic yogurt, alongside toasted bread and salata. Enjoy!

page_recipe_notes: Storage Store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 4 days. The garlic yogurt is best enjoyed immediately, but can be stored in a container in the fridge for up to 1 day.
